sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: grep
toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

toolsAdded.name: find
toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

toolsAdded.name: ls
toolsAdded.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

toolsAdded.name: ci_status
toolsAdded.description: Retrieve all current source-revision statuses and new completed CI results in one efficient call. Default cursor advances after retrieval; optional sinceSeq rereads older results.

toolsAdded.name: ci_wait
toolsAdded.description: Wait for new CI results for up to 60 seconds. Use only when useful independent coding or testing work is exhausted. Returns all current statuses and new results.

toolsAdded.name: notifications_dismiss
toolsAdded.description: Remove notification IDs together, or use ids:["*"] to remove all active notifications in this session at execution time. Retain them in history.

toolsAdded.name: notifications_history
toolsAdded.description: Retrieve previously received notifications, including dismissed entries. since is a duration like 2h.

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. `src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

# Package Catalog usage

Requires Node 24; no dependencies. Run all tests with `npm test`.

## Records and library

A record has the following shape:

```json
{"id":"tools","name":"Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["utility"],"dependencies":[]}
```

Versions use three integer components and optional prerelease (for example
`1.2.0-beta.2`), without build metadata or numeric leading zeros. IDs and names
are trimmed; tags are lowercase, trimmed, unique and sorted. Dependencies are
unique with their original order preserved. Unknown dependencies may be stored,
but dependency planning rejects missing nodes and cycles.

`createCatalog` in `src/catalog.mjs` provides list/get/add/update/remove and
atomic `applyBatch`. Returned records are independent copies. Search defaults to
id ascending, offset 0, limit 20 (maximum 100); tag filters require all tags.
`planDependencies` emits DFS dependency-first order; `reverseDependencies` gives
sorted transitive dependents.

## HTTP

The server factory returns an unlistening, in-memory HTTP server. Start it with:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e "import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs'; import {createServer} from './src/server.mjs'; createServer(createCatalog()).listen(3000);"
```

```sh
curl http://localhost:3000/health
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/records -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"tools","name":"Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["utility"],"dependencies":[]}'
curl 'http://localhost:3000/records?text=tool&tags=utility&sortBy=version&order=desc&limit=10&offset=0'
curl http://localhost:3000/records/tools
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/records/tools -d '{"name":"New Tools"}'
curl 'http://localhost:3000/plan?ids=tools'
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3000/records/tools
```

GET `/records` also accepts inclusive `versionMin`/`versionMax` bounds, sortBy
`id`, `name`, or `version`, and order `asc`/`desc`. Ties always use id ascending.
URL-encode record IDs in paths, including slashes as `%2F`.

POST creation returns 201, GET/PATCH return 200, DELETE returns 204.
Errors return JSON `{"error":"message"}`: malformed input 400, unknown route or
record 404, duplicate creation 409, bodies exceeding 1 MiB 413. Import failures
are 400 and do not partially write records. Data lasts only for the lifetime of
the catalog; HTTP does not persist the CLI file.

## CLI

`--file` is required for every command; a missing file starts with an empty
catalog. Existing files must contain a valid JSON record array.

```sh
node src/cli.mjs add --file catalog.json --record '{"id":"tools","name":"Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["utility"],"dependencies":[]}'
node src/cli.mjs list --file catalog.json --text tools --tags utility
node src/cli.mjs plan --file catalog.json --ids tools
node src/cli.mjs export-csv --file catalog.json > catalog.csv
node src/cli.mjs import-csv --file another.json --input catalog.csv
node src/cli.mjs remove --file catalog.json --id tools
```

Output is JSON (list uses the search envelope; plan uses `{ids:[...]}`;
import uses `{added:N}`), except export-csv. Writes validate completely before
writing a temporary sibling file and renaming it. Invalid records, duplicate
IDs, malformed files, unknown flags, missing arguments and failed plans exit
nonzero with stderr and leave existing data untouched.

## CSV and NDJSON

CSV uses the exact header `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`. Tags and dependencies
are pipe-separated, with empty fields representing empty arrays. CSV quoting
handles commas, double quotes, CRLF/LF and embedded newlines. Because pipes are
list separators, values containing literal pipes cannot round-trip through CSV;
use NDJSON for such records.

```sh
curl http://localhost:3000/export.csv > catalog.csv
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/import.csv --data-binary @catalog.csv
curl http://localhost:3000/export.ndjson > catalog.ndjson
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/import.ndjson --data-binary @catalog.ndjson
```

Exports return `text/csv` or `application/x-ndjson`. Imports return 201
`{added:N}` and atomically add all records, rejecting duplicates rather than
replacing existing records. NDJSON ignores empty lines and accepts a final line
without a newline.

Library streaming example:

```js
import {createReadStream} from 'node:fs';
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {importNDJSON, exportNDJSON} from './src/transfer.mjs';
const catalog = createCatalog();
await importNDJSON(createReadStream('catalog.ndjson'), catalog);
for await (const line of exportNDJSON(catalog.list())) process.stdout.write(line);
```

`importNDJSON` accepts async string/Buffer chunks and safely decodes UTF-8 even
when characters cross Buffer boundaries. Malformed JSON or invalid records
leave the entire catalog unchanged. `importCSV(text,catalog)` likewise validates
and commits atomically; both return the added normalized records.

# Package Catalog usage

Requires Node 24; no dependencies. Run all tests with `npm test`.

## Records and library

A record has the following shape:

```json
{"id":"tools","name":"Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["utility"],"dependencies":[]}
```

Versions use three integer components and optional prerelease (for example
`1.2.0-beta.2`), without build metadata or numeric leading zeros. IDs and names
are trimmed; tags are lowercase, trimmed, unique and sorted. Dependencies are
unique with their original order preserved. Unknown dependencies may be stored,
but dependency planning rejects missing nodes and cycles.

`createCatalog` in `src/catalog.mjs` provides list/get/add/update/remove and
atomic `applyBatch`. Returned records are independent copies. Search defaults to
id ascending, offset 0, limit 20 (maximum 100); tag filters require all tags.
`planDependencies` emits DFS dependency-first order; `reverseDependencies` gives
sorted transitive dependents.

## HTTP

The server factory returns an unlistening, in-memory HTTP server. Start it with:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e "import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs'; import {createServer} from './src/server.mjs'; createServer(createCatalog()).listen(3000);"
```

```sh
curl http://localhost:3000/health
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/records -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"tools","name":"Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["utility"],"dependencies":[]}'
curl 'http://localhost:3000/records?text=tool&tags=utility&sortBy=version&order=desc&limit=10&offset=0'
curl http://localhost:3000/records/tools
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/records/tools -d '{"name":"New Tools"}'
curl 'http://localhost:3000/plan?ids=tools'
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3000/records/tools
```

GET `/records` also accepts inclusive `versionMin`/`versionMax` bounds, sortBy
`id`, `name`, or `version`, and order `asc`/`desc`. Ties always use id ascending.
URL-encode record IDs in paths, including slashes as `%2F`.

POST creation returns 201, GET/PATCH return 200, DELETE returns 204.
Errors return JSON `{"error":"message"}`: malformed input 400, unknown route or
record 404, duplicate creation 409, bodies exceeding 1 MiB 413. Import failures
are 400 and do not partially write records. Data lasts only for the lifetime of
the catalog; HTTP does not persist the CLI file.

## CLI

`--file` is required for every command; a missing file starts with an empty
catalog. Existing files must contain a valid JSON record array.

```sh
node src/cli.mjs add --file catalog.json --record '{"id":"tools","name":"Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["utility"],"dependencies":[]}'
node src/cli.mjs list --file catalog.json --text tools --tags utility
node src/cli.mjs plan --file catalog.json --ids tools
node src/cli.mjs export-csv --file catalog.json > catalog.csv
node src/cli.mjs import-csv --file another.json --input catalog.csv
node src/cli.mjs remove --file catalog.json --id tools
```

Output is JSON (list uses the search envelope; plan uses `{ids:[...]}`;
import uses `{added:N}`), except export-csv. Writes validate completely before
writing a temporary sibling file and renaming it. Invalid records, duplicate
IDs, malformed files, unknown flags, missing arguments and failed plans exit
nonzero with stderr and leave existing data untouched.

## CSV and NDJSON

CSV uses the exact header `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`. Tags and dependencies
are pipe-separated, with empty fields representing empty arrays. CSV quoting
handles commas, double quotes, CRLF/LF and embedded newlines. Because pipes are
list separators, values containing literal pipes cannot round-trip through CSV;
use NDJSON for such records.

```sh
curl http://localhost:3000/export.csv > catalog.csv
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/import.csv --data-binary @catalog.csv
curl http://localhost:3000/export.ndjson > catalog.ndjson
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/import.ndjson --data-binary @catalog.ndjson
```

Exports return `text/csv` or `application/x-ndjson`. Imports return 201
`{added:N}` and atomically add all records, rejecting duplicates rather than
replacing existing records. NDJSON ignores empty lines and accepts a final line
without a newline.

Library streaming example:

```js
import {createReadStream} from 'node:fs';
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {importNDJSON, exportNDJSON} from './src/transfer.mjs';
const catalog = createCatalog();
await importNDJSON(createReadStream('catalog.ndjson'), catalog);
for await (const line of exportNDJSON(catalog.list())) process.stdout.write(line);
```

`importNDJSON` accepts async string/Buffer chunks and safely decodes UTF-8 even
when characters cross Buffer boundaries. Malformed JSON or invalid records
leave the entire catalog unchanged. `importCSV(text,catalog)` likewise validates
and commits atomically; both return the added normalized records.

# Package Catalog usage

Requires Node 24; no dependencies. Run all tests with `npm test`.

## Records and library

A record has the following shape:

```json
{"id":"tools","name":"Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["utility"],"dependencies":[]}
```

Versions use three integer components and optional prerelease (for example
`1.2.0-beta.2`), without build metadata or numeric leading zeros. IDs and names
are trimmed; tags are lowercase, trimmed, unique and sorted. Dependencies are
unique with their original order preserved. Unknown dependencies may be stored,
but dependency planning rejects missing nodes and cycles.

`createCatalog` in `src/catalog.mjs` provides list/get/add/update/remove and
atomic `applyBatch`. Returned records are independent copies. Search defaults to
id ascending, offset 0, limit 20 (maximum 100); tag filters require all tags.
`planDependencies` emits DFS dependency-first order; `reverseDependencies` gives
sorted transitive dependents.

## HTTP

The server factory returns an unlistening, in-memory HTTP server. Start it with:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e "import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs'; import {createServer} from './src/server.mjs'; createServer(createCatalog()).listen(3000);"
```

```sh
curl http://localhost:3000/health
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/records -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"tools","name":"Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["utility"],"dependencies":[]}'
curl 'http://localhost:3000/records?text=tool&tags=utility&sortBy=version&order=desc&limit=10&offset=0'
curl http://localhost:3000/records/tools
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/records/tools -d '{"name":"New Tools"}'
curl 'http://localhost:3000/plan?ids=tools'
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3000/records/tools
```

GET `/records` also accepts inclusive `versionMin`/`versionMax` bounds, sortBy
`id`, `name`, or `version`, and order `asc`/`desc`. Ties always use id ascending.
URL-encode record IDs in paths, including slashes as `%2F`.

POST creation returns 201, GET/PATCH return 200, DELETE returns 204.
Errors return JSON `{"error":"message"}`: malformed input 400, unknown route or
record 404, duplicate creation 409, bodies exceeding 1 MiB 413. Import failures
are 400 and do not partially write records. Data lasts only for the lifetime of
the catalog; HTTP does not persist the CLI file.

## CLI

`--file` is required for every command; a missing file starts with an empty
catalog. Existing files must contain a valid JSON record array.

```sh
node src/cli.mjs add --file catalog.json --record '{"id":"tools","name":"Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["utility"],"dependencies":[]}'
node src/cli.mjs list --file catalog.json --text tools --tags utility
node src/cli.mjs plan --file catalog.json --ids tools
node src/cli.mjs export-csv --file catalog.json > catalog.csv
node src/cli.mjs import-csv --file another.json --input catalog.csv
node src/cli.mjs remove --file catalog.json --id tools
```

Output is JSON (list uses the search envelope; plan uses `{ids:[...]}`;
import uses `{added:N}`), except export-csv. Writes validate completely before
writing a temporary sibling file and renaming it. Invalid records, duplicate
IDs, malformed files, unknown flags, missing arguments and failed plans exit
nonzero with stderr and leave existing data untouched.

## CSV and NDJSON

CSV uses the exact header `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`. Tags and dependencies
are pipe-separated, with empty fields representing empty arrays. CSV quoting
handles commas, double quotes, CRLF/LF and embedded newlines. Because pipes are
list separators, values containing literal pipes cannot round-trip through CSV;
use NDJSON for such records.

```sh
curl http://localhost:3000/export.csv > catalog.csv
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/import.csv --data-binary @catalog.csv
curl http://localhost:3000/export.ndjson > catalog.ndjson
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/import.ndjson --data-binary @catalog.ndjson
```

Exports return `text/csv` or `application/x-ndjson`. Imports return 201
`{added:N}` and atomically add all records, rejecting duplicates rather than
replacing existing records. NDJSON ignores empty lines and accepts a final line
without a newline.

Library streaming example:

```js
import {createReadStream} from 'node:fs';
import {createCatalog} from './src/catalog.mjs';
import {importNDJSON, exportNDJSON} from './src/transfer.mjs';
const catalog = createCatalog();
await importNDJSON(createReadStream('catalog.ndjson'), catalog);
for await (const line of exportNDJSON(catalog.list())) process.stdout.write(line);
```

`importNDJSON` accepts async string/Buffer chunks and safely decodes UTF-8 even
when characters cross Buffer boundaries. Malformed JSON or invalid records
leave the entire catalog unchanged. `importCSV(text,catalog)` likewise validates
and commits atomically; both return the added normalized records.
